text: The letter template version lives in rwb-comms and this story is the approval gate and the record: rwb-access reads the version through the P6 contract, hands the approval to the P6 approve operation, records the approving role code and the time in its own decision-record chain and answers the history from that chain; it reads no template, notice or merge-field row and holds no copy of a template body, a merge field or a template state.
why: The legacy story holds the template and the notice in one schema with the decision log, and the ownership map moves all three template tables to P6 while the metadata of this story carries no P6 contract dependency; the split between the gate and the owner of the template has to be fixed on Day 1, or the story would either invent a dependency it may not add or read a foreign table it may not read.
read: Ownership Map v1 (template, notice, merge_field = P6; API POST /admin/templates and POST /admin/templates/{templateId}/approve = P6); Architecture v5 slide 41; TSD P6 v2 T3.1 and appendix T-A API-P6-003 to API-P6-007; TSD P4 v3 T6.3; FSD P4 v3 A2.21; Template and Rules R5.4 dependency class C and R5.5 DP-01
applied_in: Section 1 Story; section 3 Preconditions; section 4 Flow steps 6 to 16; section 8 Business rule BR5; section 11 Data; section 12.2 and 12.7 Contract; section 13 Build step 3
confirm: Solution architect and the P6 rwb-comms tech lead when the P6 template contract is published
impact: If the P6 contract renames a path or a field, or answers the read by id differently, only CommsTemplateClient, its fake and the contract test change; the gate, its two refusals and the history stay as specified. The missing C dependency is added to the metadata at D1 and no template table enters rwb_access.

text: The approving role recorded on a template approval is RW-COMPLY, the role the FSD A2.21.3.3 role table names, while the right that opens the gate is Rules and parameters A of TSD P4 v3 T6.1, which that matrix gives to RW-RISK (RA) and RW-COE (CRUD) and not to RW-COMPLY (R only); the SIT approver holds RW-COMPLY and holds the A letter, and the four-eyes rule of T6.3 holds in either reading, because the author of a version can never approve it.
why: The FSD role table and the T6.1 matrix disagree on who approves a letter template, R-PREC puts the technical specification above the functional one, and a story may not change a metadata value; without a default the recorded role code, the right that is authorised and the test data would contradict one another.
read: FSD P4 v3 A2.21.3.3 roles and permissions; TSD P4 v3 T6.1 RBAC matrix; TSD P4 v3 T6.3 author and approver; legacy RWB-E8-010 permission checks (Rules and parameters C for RW-COE and A for RW-RISK); Template and Rules R3 R-PREC
applied_in: Section 3 Preconditions; section 4 Flow steps 5 and 8; section 7 Background and AC4; section 8 Business rules BR3, BR4 and BR6; section 10 Authority; section 13 Configuration and reference data
confirm: Solution architect with Compliance and the access administrator at the P4 design review
impact: If the matrix is corrected to give RW-COMPLY the A letter, or if Compliance is read to approve under the RW-RISK letter, only the role-to-letters row and the SIT test users change; the gate, the four-eyes refusal and the field that records the approving role code do not.

text: The approval history answers, for each approved version, the template version, the state APPROVED, the approving role code, the time of the approval and the approval reference, and never a name, an e-mail address or a user reference: the approver user reference that rwb-comms holds in approved_by stays with rwb-comms and is not answered by this service.
why: REQ-OCC-002 asks that the approval be recorded against the version and the template table holds the approver as a user reference (DF-REF-063), while the record of a decision may not copy personal data into its payload or its reads; a default is needed on what the history says about who approved a version.
read: TSD P6 v2 T3.1 DF-REF-063 approved_by, DF-REF-064 approved_at and DF-REF-065 valid_from; TSD P4 v3 T6.3 author and approver; REQ-OCC-002; NFR-040; the guardrails of the legacy story RWB-E8-010

impact: If audit needs the person, the answer is a second read of the rwb-comms approval and not a field of this service's record; the history fields, the entry payload and the tests do not change.
